Sports.title: Transfer Notebook: Espirito Santo could follow Bowen out of West Ham, Newcastle’s fight to keep key star, where next for Lewandowski?
Sports.content:
Transfer Notebook: Espirito Santo could follow Bowen out of West Ham, Newcastle’s fight to keep key star, where next for Lewandowski?

West Ham are set for a mass exodus if they go down - and manager Nuno Espirito Santo could be one of the first out of the door.

The Hammers are facing an uphill task to preserve their 14-year Premier League status with Tottenham effectively needing just one point to stay up at their expense.



3 West Ham could lose manager Nuno and star player and captain Jarrod Bowen if they are relegated from the Premier League Credit: Getty

Relegation would have disastrous financial implications after reporting pre-tax losses of more than £104million in their most recent accounts.

talkSPORT understands all of the Hammers’ top stars will have their wages slashed as a result of dropping into the Championship.

England forward Jarrod Bowen, Manchester United and Arsenal target Mateus Fernandes, and Crysencio Summerville are the club’s most sellable assets, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Jean-Clair Todibo will also push for moves.



Meanwhile, there is doubt over whether Espirito Santo will continue beyond the end of the season having failed to keep West Ham up.

Newcastle's battle to keep Man United target

Newcastle United face an uphill fight to keep Lewis Hall.

As previously reported in this Notebook, Hall is expected to be named in Thomas Tuchel’s England World Cup squad on Friday after a stellar season at St James' Park.



The tournament in North America will give the former Chelsea youngster the chance to enhance his growing reputation.

And sources have told talkSPORT that Hall, 21, is open to a move this summer.



Manchester United are among the clubs actively seeking a new left-back to ease the workload on Luke Shaw, and the Red Devils' director of football Jason Wilcox is a big admirer of Hall.

With £70m-rated Anthony Gordon almost certain to leave and Sandro Tonali also pushing for an exit, Newcastle are likely to battle hard to keep Hall.

3 Hall is set to go to the World Cup with England and could also bag himself a new club this summer Credit: Getty

LaLiga side eye Championship promotion hero

Ipswich promotion-winning hero Dan Neil is a target for Spanish side Valencia.



Sunderland man Neil spent the second half of the season on loan at Portman Road and helped Kieran McKenna’s men clinch a return to the Premier League on the final day.

The 24-year-old will be available as a free agent when his contract at the Stadium of Light expires this summer.

Valencia boss Carlos Corberan rates Neil highly from his time managing in the Championship at West Brom.

Where next for Lewy?

Robert Lewandowski could be the latest superstar heading to play in Saudi Arabia.



Lewandowski is leaving Barcelona with his contract expiring after scoring 119 goals in 191 games.

3 Lewandowski will be a free agent in the summer with his Barcelona exit confirmed - but where will the Polish goalmachine end up next? Credit: Getty

Despite Rio Ferdinand suggesting a possible move from Man United for the Poland goalmachine, Lewandowski has interest from Saudi sides Al Qadsiah, Al Hilal and Al Ittihad.

The 37-year-old is also wanted by ambitious MLS side Chicago Fire, who tried and failed to land Kevin de Bruyne this time last year.

Sports.title: How many clean sheets does Jordan Pickford have for England and where does he sit in all-time history?
Sports.content:
How many clean sheets does Jordan Pickford have for England and where does he sit in all-time history?

Jordan Pickford could cement himself as an England goalkeeping legend this summer at the World Cup.

The Everton keeper is already one of the best in his position for the Three Lions, having been an ever-present since 2017.

2 Pickford has been England's No.1 for almost a decade Credit: Getty

He is now set for his third World Cup representing his nation, after starting every single match at the last four major tournaments.

Along the way, Pickford has kept a huge number of clean sheets too, seeing him rise up the all-time leaderboard with ease.

How many clean sheets does Pickford have for England?

Pickford has 43 clean sheets for England in 82 appearances.

It means he boasts an impressive record of not conceding a goal in over 50 per cent of his total caps for the Three Lions.

His first clean sheet on the international stage came in November 2017 in a 0-0 draw against Germany.

And heading into the 2026 World Cup, his most recent clean sheet came against Serbia in a 2-0 victory in November 2025.

Pickford's 43 shutouts have him sitting joint-second in the all-time list of goalkeepers for England, needing one more to move up to outright second in the history books.

Ex-Manchester City shotstopper Joe Hart retired with 43.

But well clear at the top is the legendary Peter Shilton, who kept 66 clean sheets in his 125 caps for the Three Lions.

Also in the top five are former Arsenal keeper David Seaman and the iconic Gordon Banks, with 40 and 35 clean sheets respectively.

All-time most clean sheets for England Peter Shilton - 66 clean sheets Jordan Pickford / Joe Hart - 43 clean sheets David Seaman - 40 clean sheets Gordon Banks - 35 clean sheets Ray Clemence - 27 clean sheets Chris Woods - 26 clean sheets Paul Robinson - 24 clean sheets David James - 21 clean sheets Nigel Martyn - 13 clean sheets Harry Hibbs - 10 clean sheets

2 Pickford has 43 clean sheets for England, with seven of those coming at World Cups Credit: Getty

Pickford at the World Cup

The 2026 World Cup will be Pickford's third of his career, having appeared for England in the 2018 and 2022 tournaments.

He played every game at both of those, featuring in 12 matches in total in the iconic competition over the last eight years.

When it comes to clean sheets, he has four at World Cups.

His first came against Belgium in 2018, while his most recent clean sheet at the tournament was a 3-0 win over Senegal in 2022.

Pickford's four World Cup clean sheets see him hunting down the leading pack of historic goalkeepers.

Shilton has the most ever for England in the competition with 10, and that also has him tied for the most ever at World Cups.

Fabian Barthez also has 10, with Jan Jongbloed, Leao, Sepp Maier, Taffarel and Hugo Lloris joint-second with eight each.

Thibaut Courtois, Iker Casillas and Manuel Neuer all have seven each, as Pickford looks to catch them with some more this summer.

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim closing in top European job just four months after Man United sack
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim closing in top European job just four months after Man United sack

Add us as preferred source

Ruben Amorim is set to replace Jose Mourinho as Benfica manager.

It would be his first managerial role since he was sacked by Manchester United in January.

3 Amorim is in line to be named Benfica manager four months after his United sacking Credit: Getty

Mourinho is closing in on a return to Real Madrid this summer and has agreed a two-year contract.

His exit from Benfica could open the door for Amorim's appointment, talkSPORT understands.

The former United boss is admired by club president Rui Costa despite his struggles at Old Trafford.

Amorim played for Benfica during Costa's time as sporting director before moving into management.

Fulham boss Marco Silva had previously emerged as a candidate to succeed Mourinho.

The Portuguese is out of contract at Craven Cottage at the end of the season.

However, the Cottagers are growing increasingly confident Silva will sign a new deal, talkSPORT understands.

Amorim at Benfica

Amorim spent nine years with Benfica as a player after joining the club in 2008.

The former midfielder went on to make 154 appearances, scoring six goals and adding 14 assists.

He also won 11 trophies during his time at Benfica, including three league titles.

3 Amorim spent nine years with Benfica during his playing career Credit: Getty

Amorim ultimately ended his career with the club, retiring in 2017 aged 32.

The 41-year-old quickly turned to coaching with spells as manager of Casa Pia and Braga in his native Portugal.

However, he later took charge of Benfica's bitter city rivals Sporting Lisbon in 2020.

Across four years as Sporting boss, Amorim won two league titles.

United woes

His results with the club would earn a move to United in November 2024.

Although he reached the Europa League final last season, he was unable to prevent the club from recording a 15th place finish.

3 Amorim won two Portuguese titles during his time in charge of Sporting Credit: Getty

It represented the Red Devils' lowest-ever Premier League finish as well as their lowest top-flight points tally for 51 years.

Following their failure to qualify for Europe, United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Grimsby Town in August.

Amorim was subsequently sacked in January before being replaced by Michael Carrick until the end of the season.

Carrick has since secured Champions League qualification and is set to be appointed on a permanent basis.

Sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz WITHDRAWS from Wimbledon with two-time SW19 champion still sidelined by injury after skipping the French Open
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz WITHDRAWS from Wimbledon with two-time SW19 champion still sidelined by injury after skipping the French Open

Two-time Wimbledon champion Carlos Alcaraz has confirmed that he will not enter this year's Championships due to the persistent wrist injury that has kept him from competing at the French Open.

The record-breaking Spaniard announced last month that he would be unable to defend his title in Paris at the end of May as it was the 'most prudent' decision to ensure his recovery.

But there will be some concern for fans of the former world No1 after Alcaraz announced that he is still not able to play competitive tennis.

'My recovery is going well and I'm feeling much better, but unfortunately I'm still not ready to play, so I have to withdraw from the grass-court swing at Queen's and Wimbledon,' Alcaraz shared in a brief statement on social media.

'They're two really special tournaments for me and I'll miss them loads. We keep working to get back as soon as possible (red heart emoji).'

Alcaraz has missed large chunks of the clay season, having last featured in Barcelona where he was forced to withdraw before his match against Tomas Machac – although the 23-year-old did make sure he made the final at the sole event he completed, April's Monte-Carlo Masters.

Carlos Alcaraz has confirmed that he will miss out on the grass court season entirely as he recovers from a wrist injury

The Spaniard's high profile absence robs him of the opportunity to snatch back his Wimbledon title from last year's winner Jannik Sinner

Now, the star will miss out on the entirety of the grass season, including the opportunity to defend his title at Queen's Club in June, and wrestle back his Centre Court crown from world No1 Jannik Sinner.

Last year, Sinner brought Alcaraz's prodigal Wimbledon run to a halt as he sought his just revenge after their all-timer of a Grand Slam final at Roland-Garros one month earlier.

But with the two superstars at the very top of the men's game content to pass major titles between them due to their lack of serious rivals elsewhere in the tour, Alcaraz will no doubt be upset to miss out on the opportunity to reassert his grass-dominance.

From Sinner's perspective, there seems little impediment to the Italian enjoying a clean sweep in Alcaraz's absence.

Going into the French Open on Sunday, the 24-year-old is now 29 matches unbeaten and picked up two Masters titles in the process.

Sinner also matched Novak Djokovic's superlative record to become the second man to win all nine ATP 1000 tournaments.

As well as the rest of the chasing pack eager for a chance to break Alcaraz and Sinner's scarcely believable dominance, the Serbian superstar will be one of the more interested parties in the Spaniard's bombshell news.

Djokovic remains just one Grand Slam title away from shattering Margaret Court's long-standing record, with Tim Henman sharing on Tuesday that if the veteran is to find a breakthrough, it is likely to be on a favourable surface.

'I think Djokovic no doubt has a chance at Wimbledon because the physical demands on grass are less than on clay,' Henman told TNT Sport. 'So, for me, at Djokovic's age, for him to win seven best-of-five-set matches on clay at Roland-Garros, I find that hard to believe.

'Whereas on grass, given his pedigree, and there are fewer players that are comfortable on grass, I definitely would give him a shot at Wimbledon.'



Djokovic defeated Sinner in five gruelling sets at this year's Australian Open before he was downed in four by eventual champion Alcaraz.

Sports.title: Row erupts over Enzo Maresca to Man City with Chelsea threatening legal action if they don't pay up compensation for their former manager to replace Pep Guardiola
Sports.content:
Chelsea are set to demand compensation from Manchester City should they appoint Enzo Maresca – and take legal action if it is not forthcoming.

Stamford Bridge officials were left incensed with the Italian amid allegations he had spoken with City while still in post with them.

And with Maresca, who subsequently departed in acrimonious circumstances, now set to replace Pep Guardiola – whose exit Daily Mail Sport revealed last night – Chelsea are primed for action.

Should a figure not be agreed, the west London club could then complain to the Premier League, which would then investigate.

Last month, at a conference in Los Angeles, Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali was asked about Maresca's exit.

'The change wasn't the club's decision,' he said, 'for reasons I can't speak about legally'.

Enzo Maresca looks set to take over as Man City boss from Pep Guardiola

Guardiola, Erling Haaland and Maresca are pictured together while the Italian was at Chelsea

Perhaps tellingly, Eghbali added: 'I think the reasons will become kind of clear in due course. But no, it's not a change we wanted to make. It's a change that's had a bit of a negative impact on the season, when you're changing systems and personnel. And it's one we've got to fight our way out of.'

Maresca left Chelsea on January 2 with his position viewed as untenable after he skipped post-match media duties following a draw with Bournemouth.

The club has been in second place before a run of poor results that preceded his departure.

Replacement Liam Rosenior was unable to turn things around and the club now has a caretaker manager in charge for the remainder of what has been a deeply disappointing campaign.

Before joining Leicester City, Maresca was City's Under 23s coach and then first team assistant to Guardiola in 2022-23.

After guiding the Foxes to the Championship he won the UEFA Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup while at Chelsea.

His relationship with the club, however, deteriorated. This newspaper revealed Chelsea bosses had taken the extraordinary measure of placing a member of medical staff on the bench during games to ensure Maresca took players who were returning from injury off at pre-agreed times.

Alarm bells had initially sounding after December's win against Everton, when Maresca described the preceeding 48 hours as his 'worst' at Chelsea due to a lack of 'support'.

Maresca was previously part of Guardiola's backroom staff at the Etihad Stadium

He later refused to clarify the comments, which were revealed as aimed at the medical team guidelines, with acrimony bubbling as the Blues' form worsened.

Speculation had been rife that Maresca would eventually become Guardiola's successor due to their spell working together, even during his time in the Chelsea dugout.

As reports emerged days after the Everton victory in December that Guardiola was considering leaving at the end of the season, Maresca was keen to stress that he did not 'pay attention' to the links.

‘I'm focused on the Newcastle game,' Maresca said at the time. 'I'm focused on my job.

'Again, I signed a contract last year until 2029. I'm happy with that, and no more than that.

‘It doesn't affect me at all because I know that is 100 per cent speculation. In this moment, there is no time for these kind of things. First of all, because I have a contract here until 2029 probably. My focus is just about this club and I'm very proud to be here. Again, it's speculation.'

But such speculation was only inflamed by a change of personnel in Maresca's camp, with the Italian choosing to be represented by super-agent Jorge Mendes in the wake of winning the Club World Cup.

City are to host a parade this weekend on Monday, at which fans are expected to be given the opportunity to say farewell to Guardiola, who has won 17 major trophies during a decade of dominance at the Etihad Stadium.

His side head to Bournemouth tonight knowing that anything other than victory would hand the title to rivals Arsenal.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso's 'first Chelsea signing' announces exit from his club ahead of summer transfer to Stamford Bridge
Sports.content:
The man tipped to be Xabi Alonso's first signing as Chelsea manager has announced he will be leaving Strasbourg at the end of the season.

Valentin Barco has been heavily linked with a move to Stamford Bridge, and he has revealed that he will not be playing for the French side - Chelsea's sister club - next season ahead of his expected move.

The midfielder wrote on Instagram: 'Today I have to say goodbye to this club, which I joined with great enthusiasm. In this year and a half, I've had some wonderful times, including the best day of our lives, March 28, 2025, the day Gemma was born.

'I always gave my all on the pitch in every match for this shirt. I want to thank my team-mates who made everything easier for me, Liam and his staff for the trust they placed in me and for making me the player I am, Gary and his staff for understanding me and helping me improve, everyone who works at the club and supports us every day, and the fans for the affection they have always shown me.

'From afar, I will support you and cheer you on so you always win. I am incredibly grateful to Strasbourg, and my family and I will return whenever we can; it's a very special place in our lives.'

'Thank you so much for this year and a half, and best of luck for the future. Thank you Strasbourg.'

Valentin Barco (right), who is expected to be Xabi Alonso's first signing as Chelsea boss, has announced he is leaving Strasbourg

Alonso has a long to-do list with the Blues and is expected to be busy in the transfer market

Barco, who joined the club from Brighton - initially on loan - in February last year, can play in either midfield or at left back. In his post, he referenced former Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior, who coached the club before his move to the Blues.

He is now expected to join the Blues and become Alonso's first signing when he takes over in the summer.

Daily Mail Sport has been told Alonso liked what he heard during his interview process, led by the club’s co-sporting directors, Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart, and that all soon realised they were aligned when discussing what they need to do to be successful.

Chelsea even offered to name Alonso their ‘manager’ rather than ‘head coach’ after promising him more power than their previous appointments. The former Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid boss will be an equal partner alongside their sporting leadership team and ownership.

He is expected to be busy in the transfer market, in terms of both incomings and outgoings. There is plenty of dead wood to chop - especially if he wants to bring players in.

It's understood that the Spaniard has also been tasked with changing the culture around the club, as well as improving top stars who have struggled to impress this season.

Sports.title: Hundreds of dodgy Fire Stick and TV box users identified and warned they have just two weeks to stop illegally watching Premier League football or face legal action
Sports.content:
Hundreds of users of dodgy box and Fire Sticks have been warned they could face legal action from Sky.

The broadcaster has sent letters to addresses in Ireland, giving individuals two weeks to provide a written commitment not to stream content illegally again.

Should individuals fail to respond or break the promise, Sky state it will consider legal action against them.

The warning comes after the Irish High Court ruled in March that names and addresses of over 300 'dodgy box' users would be handed over to Sky in efforts to clamp down on illegal streaming.

Sky had launched civil action against Revolut Bank UAB, after 304 subscribers had used the banking app to pay resellers of pirated content.

The broadcaster had sought a Norwich Pharmacal order, which allows information to be obtained from third parties who have become 'mixed up' in wrongdoing.

Hundreds of users of dodgy box and Fire Sticks have been warned they could face legal action in letters by Sky

Broadcasters have been seeking to take legal action against illegal streamers and resellers

The move raised the prospect of those watching Premier League football illegally through 'dodgy boxes' and 'dodgy Fire Sticks' being identified and prosecuted.

'Sky can confirm it has issued a first wave of cease-and-desist letters to c.200 individuals who paid for an unlawful subscription to the illegal IPTV is Easy service,' a Sky spokesperson told the Irish Times.

'Where an individual does not engage with us following receipt of this letter, Sky is prepared to pursue legal action.

'This may include seeking an injunction, damages arising from the infringement, and recovery of legal costs.'

The Irish Times reported that Sky had informed the recipients of the letter that it believes they have purchased a subscription 'providing access to an app and/or streaming device (such as modified Amazon Fire TV Sticks or similar) that allows people to watch Sky channels (and others) without having a Sky subscription.

'This is illegal as Sky owns the legal rights to the Sky channels.'

The warning, which Sky stated should be considered a 'legal letter', called on the recipients 'to stop using illegal IPTV services and to turn off your access to any such services immediately'.

Many UK-based illegal streaming accounts utilise feeds from Irish Sky boxes, Daily Mail Sport understands.

'Dodgy boxes' and illegal Fire Sticks are streaming devices that have third-party software installed in them, allowing users to watch premium content from providers such as TNT Sports, Sky Sports and Disney+ for free.

The use of these devices is deemed a 'serious crime', and police forces across the UK and Ireland, alongside the Federation Against Copyright Theft (FACT), have been targeting individuals who continue to watch unauthorised content.

Sky, who pay billions to the Premier League to show matches, also have their own in-house piracy team.

Police have warned that the purchasing of Fire Sticks and dodgy boxes 'often helps fund organised crime', and the streaming software installed on the devices often leads to personal information becoming compromised, including banking details.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson sensationally claims he caught Brad Pitt with his ex-wife in wild tale
Sports.content:
Mike Tyson sensationally claims he caught Brad Pitt with his ex-wife in wild tale

Mike Tyson has recalled the remarkable day he caught his ex-wife with a young Brad Pitt as their marriage was spiraling towards divorce.

The former world heavyweight champion told the wild tale during an appearance on 'This Past Weekend,' a podcast hosted by Theo Von.

Tyson, now 59, was asked if anyone had ever stolen his girlfriend. He recalled the time he spotted his ex-wife Robin Givens with Pitt - before the actor became a Hollywood sensation.

'That's an interesting story. He didn't steal her from me, but me and my wife were going through a divorce,' recalled Tyson, who married the actress in 1988 before they divorced a year later.

At that time, Iron Mike claimed, he and Givens were sleeping together by night while 'fighting in the papers' by day.

'But, one day, I went over to the house... she wasn't home. Nobody,' Tyson continued. 'Then, [I saw her] driving up the road with the BMW that I bought her.' Tyson spotted someone else in the car.

Boxing legend Mike Tyson is pictured with his ex-wife, Robin Givens, back in May 1988

Tyson claims he once caught Givens with Brad Pitt - before he became a Hollywood sensation

The most recent fight of Tyson's dramatic boxing career came against YouTuber Jake Paul

'I thought it was one of her friends from "Head of the Class" [the sitcom Givens appeared in as Darlene Merriman between 1986 and 1991].

'But it wasn't one of her friends. It was Brad Pitt trying to get some head,' Tyson recalled. 'He wasn't Brad Pitt yet. I didn't know who the f*** he was... he didn't even have a car.'

It is not the first time that Tyson has told a version of the story. He once claimed that he was 'mad as hell' after spotting Pitt, who back then 'was like a beach bum, a little nerdy.'

'You had to see the look on his face. He looked like he was ready to receive his last rites,' Tyson wrote in his 2013 book, Undisputed Truth. By 1989, Tyson was world heavyweight champion and considered 'The Baddest Man on the Planet.'



Givens has addressed the alleged incident in the past, admitting that Tyson saw her 'pulling up in the driveway' with Pitt.

Sports.title: Glamorous golf influencer Paige Spiranac gets hit with warning on latest social media post
Sports.content:
Glamorous golf influencer Paige Spiranac gets hit with warning on latest social media post



Golf's glamour girl Paige Spiranac is known for her often racy social media content, however, one post was slapped with a warning for a bizarre reason this week.

Spiranac, 33, has built a social media empire, amassing a staggering 11.6 million followers - four million of which come from Instagram alone.

She has become one of the biggest and most influential names in the sport without ever playing on the women's top professional circuit, the LPGA Tour, thanks to her cheeky and sexy social media posts.

However, one of her most recent posts deviated from her usual scantily-clad content - and yet, still managed to get flagged.

The former college golfer shared a video to X showing herself hitting a shot from the range on Monday morning.

Spiranac was relatively covered up for the practice session, wearing a floral print dress with a pastel pink long-sleeved shirt underneath as she left only her toned legs on show.

I know my swing is so pure it’s sexual but to have an age restriction on this post where I’m the most covered up I’ve ever been is wild lol https://t.co/V2hkrEfbbu — Paige Spiranac (@PaigeSpiranac) May 18, 2026

Golf's glamour girl Paige Spiranac's video of her swing was hit with an age warning

Spiranac, 33, has built a social media empire, amassing a staggering 11.6 million followers

Yet, despite the family-friendly attire, Spiranac's post still managed to attract censorship from X with the social media platform slapped with an age restriction.

The age warning stunned fans with many questioning why it was labeled as adult content.

'Why is this ID'ed as 'Adult Content'. I mean, you are a grown-up and so am I, but I'd say that's actually a little more conservative than most everything else you post...,' one baffled fan questioned.

Spiranac herself even poked fun at the bizarre warning, joking that the impressiveness of her swing was to blame.

'I know my swing is so pure it's sexual but to have an age restriction on this post where I'm the most covered up I've ever been is wild lol,' she wrote.

Often viewed as a polarizing figure in the world of golf - especially in the women's game - Spiranac has been forced to endure her fair share of criticism.

However, brushing it off, she has become a trailblazer, with her numbers surpassing even those of reigning Masters champion Rory McIlroy or 15-time major winner Tiger Woods.

However, Spiranac recently admitted that her rise to fame hasn't been easy. Speaking to Golf Monthly earlier this year, she confessed that she has often felt misunderstood and been left trapped by her bombshell online persona.

'It's hard to dive into all the intricacies of how this has come to be and how I feel about it, because I can see it from a feminist perspective, but I can also feel trapped sometimes. They all work together,' she said, when asked if she feels that her social media aesthetic constricts her.

The social media star has become one of the biggest and most influential names in the sport

The American is renowned for her racy content, often appearing scantily-clad in posts

Spiranac explained that part of that complexity is the scrutiny from strangers over aspects of her appearance that are out of her control.

She shared that taking ownership of her body and her looks by crafting her online persona has helped to empower her.

'It was very empowering for me to take control over my image and of my body,' she told the outlet, 'because it can be quite exhausting for people to judge you based on the way that you were shaped.



'You know, I can't help my chest size. I can't help these certain attributes of myself. And it made me almost feel dirty or ashamed of my skin and the body that I was in.'

Gary Neville, Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira are among the high-profile names to lend their insight and expertise throughout the 104-game bonanza, while the network has also landed former Spurs boss Ange Postecoglou.

There is no room, however, for Eni Aluko. The former England Lioness has been overlooked while Ian Wright - whom she controversially accused of 'blocking' broadcasting opportunities for female pundits in women's sport - has been called up.

Aluko worked for ITV at the last World Cup in 2022 but has not been selected this time.

Mark Pougatch and Laura Woods are set to lead the coverage, with Pougatch taking the lead for England's matches.

ITV have gone all out and will be based in a studio in New York with a dramatic view of Brooklyn Bridge and the Big Apple's iconic skyline.

The channel's approach is a contrast to that of the BBC, who will not have a studio in the US and who are not planning on sending their top pundits until the quarter-final stage.

ITV have confirmed their line-up for their coverage of this summer's World Cup

Eni Aluko is not among the pundits on the list - despite working for ITV at the last World Cup

That decision has been criticised by former Match of the Day presenter Gary Lineker, who described their studio as 'a green box in Salford'.

ITV will air 51 matches throughout the tournament, and have amassed an eclectic array of pundits to ensure all bases are covered.

Alongside channel stalwarts like Keane and Wright, former Chelsea manager Emma Hayes, Duncan Ferguson, Karen Carney, Patrick Vieira, Bradley Wright-Phillips, and Juan Mata will flesh out a stacked cast.

The broadcaster will also look to harness their on-the-ground advantages with additional segments from their studio in Brooklyn, led by Adam Richman of Man Vs Food fame.



Alongside co-presenter Semra Hunter, Richman will aim to give viewers a third eye on the tournament, with a socio-cultural bent.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola is seen for the first time since news of him quitting as Man City manager broke - in his own branded jacket - hours before Arsenal could win the title if his team slip up
Sports.content:
Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has been seen out in Manchester for the first time since Daily Mail Sport reported on Monday that he is set to leave the club at the end of the season.

Guardiola, 55, is expected to depart following Sunday’s final Premier League match against Aston Villa, bringing an end to a remarkable decade in charge.

During that time, the Spaniard led City to six league titles - including an unprecedented four in succession - and delivered the club’s first Champions League triumph.

Daily Mail Sport chief sports writer Oliver Holt revealed that, although the news has yet to be formally confirmed by either the club or Guardiola himself, it has been an open secret among those close to him. Confirmation is expected on Sunday, ahead of a planned open-top bus parade on Monday to celebrate his impact on English football.

And photographs exclusively obtained by Daily Mail Sport show Guardiola in public for the first time since the story broke, walking through Manchester.

He wore a limited-edition black Puma hoodie - featuring a gold ‘P’ to mark his 10th anniversary at City - with grey chinos and white trainers, and appeared sombre as he stepped away from his electric BYD car.

Photographs obtained by Daily Mail Sport show Guardiola in public for the first time since the story broke that he would be leaving City

Guardiola wore a limited-edition black Puma hoodie - featuring a gold ‘P’ to mark his 10th anniversary at City - with grey chinos, appearing sombre as he stepped away from his car

Join the discussion How will Guardiola's exit change the future of Manchester City and the Premier League?

While the news may come as a shock, succession planning is already underway. Daily Mail Sport understands that City have begun informing sponsors that an announcement is imminent.

The parade is expected to start in Manchester’s Northern Quarter at 4pm and finish outside the Colin Bell Stand reception at the Etihad Stadium around an hour later.

Guardiola’s future has been the subject of speculation for months, with the Catalan considering bringing his time at City to a close. Guardiola has one year remaining on his contract, something he has frequently alluded to, and he could yet remain at the club in another role.

Potential successors include former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca and Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany.

City head into the final week of the season on the back of a 1-0 FA Cup final win over Chelsea at Wembley, while still chasing the Premier League title. However, Arsenal’s victory over Burnley on Monday means the race will stay out of City’s hands for the remainder of the season.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed on Monday evening that Guardiola will leave City this summer

The Spaniard joined the club in 2016 and has won 17 major trophies with the club

The Gunners need only beat Crystal Palace next weekend to secure their first title in 22 years.

City face Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium on Tuesday before hosting Aston Villa at the Etihad on Sunday.

Speaking prior to Daily Mail Sport's exclusive bombshell, Guardiola said he does not demand huge fanfare on the day he departs the club.

‘The club don’t have to do anything, honestly,’ Guardiola, who has yet to officially confirm his departure, said. ‘The important thing in our lives is that when you look back, you can look with a big smile and say “that was good”.

‘Bernardo (Silva) and John (Stones) can feel that. We spoke about it over the last few days. When you’re old, a grandfather, you can look at the memories. That is the most important thing in life.’

Tired of addressing his contractual situation, Guardiola added with a dose of sarcasm: ‘Whatever happens at the end of the season – and when I extend my contract for three more years – I can look back and say, “how nice has that been?”

‘That is the most important thing by far. Most of the people who lived this time here together can feel it.’

Guardiola has told those players to seize the moment and leave nothing out there in their quest to haul in Arsenal during the final week. City have won three league titles (2019, 2022 and 2024) on the last day under the 55-year-old.

‘I prefer it to be in our control,’ he said. ‘But you never know. The important thing is to be there. I remember Johan Cruyff before (similar) games (at Barcelona) said “win our games, it's not in our hands.”

‘We cannot lose the Premier League because they don't win and we don't win. That just cannot happen. We have to. Let's win the game to arrive at the last chance and after that, guys, win our game. After that, it's not in our control. Wait.’

Sports.title: Darren Barker to take on epic 1,800-mile challenge in honour of Ricky Hatton
Sports.content:
Darren Barker to take on epic 1,800-mile challenge in honour of Ricky Hatton

Former boxing world champion Barker has revealed he will take part in a world‑first endurance challenge in honour of the late Ricky Hatton - who was sadly found dead in his home last September

View 2 Images Boxing legend Darren Barker has revealed he will embark on a 1,800-mile challenge in honour of the late Ricky Hatton

Darren Barker has revealed he will take part in a gruelling, world-first, endurance challenge in honour of the late Ricky Hatton.

‌



The former IBF middleweight champion will travel more than 1,800 miles across land and sea, beginning in August, embarking on a multi-week journey designed to push endurance and mental strength to the limits. The challenge, dubbed 'The Longest Round,' will see the popular DAZN commentator raise awareness for two men’s mental health charities - The Ricky Hatton Foundation and CALM (Campaign Against Living Miserably).

‌



Barker's journey will consist of four stages, combining long‑distance cycling with 'two of the world’s most iconic open‑water swims.' The 44-year-old will cycle from Edinburgh to Dover, before swimming the English Channel. Then, he will cycle from Calais to Gibraltar, before a nine-mile open-water swim across the Strait of Gibraltar into Morocco.

‌



'The Longest Round' was inspired by the former boxer's final interview with Hatton just days before the Mancunian's tragic death. The 'Hitman' was found hanged at his home on September 14 last year. His body was found in the games room of his £1.7 million mansion in Hyde, Greater Manchester.

"Last September I sat down to interview the legend Ricky Hatton. Little did I know that five days later Ricky would be gone. It was heartbreaking and cruel", said Barker. “As the last person to interview ‘The Hitman’, I feel there is now a message to carry — about silent struggle and breaking that silence.

‌



“'The Longest Round' is about awareness, endurance and resilience. This challenge is bigger than sport. Strength isn’t silence. Strength is speaking. Strength is asking for help. Strength is showing up for others.” Throughout the journey, Barker will be joined at various points by big names, including: Eddie Hearn, Tony Bellew, Joe Calzaghe, Carl Frampton, John Terry, Luke Littler and Henry Pollock.

Barker added: “I hope I’ll be doing Ricky proud. I’m incredibly grateful to DAZN, Matchroom Boxing, our charity partners and everyone supporting this journey.”

View 2 Images The challenge was inspired by Barker’s final interview with Hatton just days before the boxing legend's death (Image: @firstroundtv/Youtube)

‌



Back in March, senior coroner Alison Mutch said she was not satisfied Hatton intended to take his own life as he was “clearly a man who was looking forwards and making plans”. Ricky’s son Campbell, 24, and other family members burst into tears as she said there was no evidence he had “any intention to take his own life”.

Campbell revealed to the hearing that his dad was the “best he’d been in years and made massive plans for the future” which made them believe his death was “not premeditated”. The coroner said Ricky’s family had: “Lost a much loved family member and were still grieving.” He had “incredible success in his career as a boxer but his family remained the most important thing in his life” and it was “very clear that his family loved him very much”.

Ricky was found to be suffering from a degenerative brain disease before his death. Post-mortem evidence found signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in former world boxing champion Hatton, the inquest into his death heard. Analysis of his brain revealed “degenerative changes" often seen in older individuals and linked to conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease.

Article continues below

Experts revealed to the hearing that the findings were consistent with CTE associated with repeated trauma to the brain - leading to memory loss and cognitive impairment. That said, the damage was not considered to have contributed to his death.

Sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz ruled out of Wimbledon as world No2 drops heartbreaking statement
Sports.content:

Spanish star Carlos Alcaraz will not compete at Wimbledon this summer due to a wrist injury, and the two-time champion has spoken out on social media about his tough call

View 2 Images Carlos Alcaraz will not feature at Wimbledon this summer

Carlos Alcaraz has confirmed that he will not compete at Wimbledon this summer as he continues to recover from a wrist injury. The 2023 and 2024 champion has already been forced to miss one grand slam this year, having withdrawn from the French Open which will get underway later this month.

‌



The world No.2 took to social media on Tuesday to provide an update on his injury recovery, as well as state that he will not compete for a third Wimbledon title come June.

‌



“My recovery is going well and I’m feeling much better, but unfortunately I’m still not ready to compete, which is why I have to withdraw from the grass-court swing at Queen’s and Wimbledon,” Alcaraz posted on Instagram.

‌



“They are two truly special tournaments for me and I will miss them a lot. We’ll keep working to come back as soon as possible!”

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr's dad issues brutal verdict on son - 'Shot and spent'
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr's dad issues brutal verdict on son - 'Shot and spent'

The British star looked a shadow of his former self against Conor Benn in his last fight and has since been urged to retire from the sport of boxing

View Image Chris Eubank Jr with his dad Chris Sr (Image: Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

Chris Eubank Jr has been brutally told by his own father that he's 'spent' as a boxer.

‌



The 36-year-old was beaten convincingly in his last fight, dropping a points defeat to Conor Benn in November at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Benn's win came seven months on from his narrow loss to Eubank Jr at the same venue.

‌



Soon after the defeat, Eubank Jr revealed he was dealing with several health issues in the build-up to the fight, as well as posting a worrying photo of himself lying in a hospital bed not long after the sequel in north London. The Brit has since been taking some time away from the ring.

‌



Earlier this year, Eubank Jr announced that he had become a dad to two boys, hailing it as the 'greatest achievement' after their birth. Many have urged him to retire, and enjoy the precious time with his children. His father, Chris Eubank Sr, has admitted that his son's best days are behind him.

"You cannot pour riches or wisdom into vessels which think they are full. He thinks he's full. And what can I do? So the trauma that I'm experiencing before this [fight], I try not to watch it because I don't want to go back into that state of mind. It's traumatising," he told Playbook Boxing.

‌



"He’s shot. He’s spent. The boxing authorities, the boxing experts, everyone can see it, but no one's paying attention to it. And I'm not going to be a party to that. I've got to stay alone. I’ve got to stay the lone ranger, for the rules. Only when the rules come back can we then produce a calibre of fighter that can excite us. I'm not talking about one or two, when we used to produce 15, 20, when we had the Fantastic Four, we had the eras of boxing. I have given my life to this. I only can wish Junior luck and mercy. It’s a very tricky world and it hasn't changed, yet. There's a change coming."

Eubank Sr, 59, is even worried his son will decide to continue with boxing. "Of course," he added. "I've learned the hard way. When someone doesn't want you… I can't have a relationship with you if you don't take my advice. I've got to talk to you about something. And all I have to give you is advice." Eubank Jr has had a rather fractured relationship with his father before repairing it last year ahead of his first fight with Benn.

Despite calls to retire, boxing promoter Ben Shalom provided an update on Eubank Jr's future earlier this year, stating that British star could return to the ring this summer. "He's had a lot of stuff to do medically to flush out what he's been dealing with," he said. "Once that's done, he will be back, probably at 168lb, but there was an underlying issue he had to get rid of. We're looking forward to him being back in the middle of the year.

"There wasn't enough time between April and what ended up November, but initially September, to sort out the issue, it was something that required proper medical attention and he didn't get that. But now he's getting that sorted. He lives the life and then he can come back in a healthy and safe safe way. But until that's completely resolved then he wont again in a ring. But from the procedures and everything that he's had so far, it's looking like he'll make a full recovery." He added: "When you offer fighters loads of money to do stupid things, that's what they do.

"Unfortunately it is. That's where it takes the regulator to say it shouldn't be allowed. I regret seeing it, but ultimately the fighters have that choice over their own body and there's only so much you can do. It won't happen again. But I wouldn't want to see it again in boxing to be honest. I think it's really dangerous and will lead to something pretty bad."

Sports.title: 'I went viral for one-second KO - here's how I did it'
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: 'I went viral for one-second KO - here's how I did it'

Rising German boxing prospect Viktor Jurk announced himself on the world stage last week after knocking out his rival with just one punch

View 3 Images Undefeated boxing star Viktor Jurk is one of the most talked about fighters on the planet right now

Boxing star Viktor Jurk was planning on making a splash online with his unique ring walk - but it was ultimately his fists that captured the interest of millions.

‌



The 26-year-old German has established himself as a real knockout artist since his professional debut five years ago, but has yet to get any recognition - until now. Jurk made the walk to the professional ring for the 14th time last Friday, taking on Edwin Castillo on the Paddy Donovan vs Karen Chukhadzhian undercard over in Mannheim, Germany.

‌



While most fighters tend to use the opening three minutes to establish control and work their way into a contest, Jurk wasted no time in chasing a statement victory. The German giant rushed to the centre of the ring and detonated a left hand just over a second into the clash, and sent Colombian foe Edwin Castillo tumbling to the canvas.

‌



The jaw-dropping shot left Castillo in a terrifying state, as the referee waved off the contest moments later. It did not take long for the knockout to go viral - with the brutal stoppage being shared by millions worldwide. Jurk's eye-catching win was even shared by the official WorldStar Instagram account to its 43.8million followers.

Alternatively, the fight is included at no extra cost with DAZN Ultimate for £22.99 per month with a new introductory offer.

With the youngster's social following increasing by the day, Jurk admits he had been discussing ways to make a name for himself online with his inner circle. Much to his surprise, rather than his unique ring walk, it was actually his destructive power that amassed millions of views.

‌



The 6'9 behemoth revealed exclusively to Mirror Fighting: "We've been talking over last couple of months, how we can make sure I go viral on Instagram. We had some couple ideas. We thought first, it's going to be viral with with my ring entrance, because you never had someone walking in with a robot. But it was the KO. You know, it was just the work.

"And I said to them, 'Listen, I become famous with my work.' And it happened. So, yeah. It's cool. I'm happy. I'm very blessed that people start to recognise me because I have been in this game for 16 years, and now I am loving the love I get."

View 3 Images Jurk knocked Colombian Edwin Castillo just seconds into their heavyweight fight

‌



He added: "I hope my opponent is cool. I hope he's good, because in the ring, I didn't realise what I did. Now, over the days when it calms down, you realise, 'All right, damn, that was a shot.' And I hope he's good and back home. I still try to realise things what's happening right now, because this thing went too viral, to be honest.

"People recognise me on the streets. Like, they knew me before as well, back home, but now they they really recognise me. Like, it's a massive, massive, massive video clip. And I've seen my friends say, "Man, you now world star," because WorldStar put it on his f****** Instagram. It's too funny."

‌

Tyson Fury explains exactly how he will beat Anthony Joshua READ MORE :

Despite all the attention and recognition in the streets of his beloved Germany, Jurk states he is trying to remain grounded, and claims nothing much has really changed. "My life didn't change. I still live in my flat back home. I still drive my car. I still I'm able to breathe. I'm still a normal human. But, the world sees you different. It's It's just the people how they recognise you, but I'm still I'm still the same kid from my home.

"I still always I always try to ground myself. I always tell me, 'Listen, you still a kid, dream chasing. It's just a part of the process,' because how can I say I'm famous if I say people like AJ (Anthony Joshua) are famous? It just went viral, but in 1 week, it's probably... everyone forget about it.

"I enjoy the moment, but to be honest, I like to be still a normal person. I don't like to be staying in the middle position. I'm not that type of guy. I'm I'm cool. I'm always like 'When I step in the room, the people recognise me because I'm tall, I'm huge, I'm big.' So, it's it's always been like that. But now, they start to know you from the work, so, okay, it's cool. But, still, I try to make sure I stay with my my own people and just stay humble. That's it."

‌



View 3 Images The German star extended his record to 14-0 following the one-punch KO in front of his home fans

Jurk admits the plan was to actually get a few rounds under his belt in order to get some crucial minutes in, but when the opportunity presented itself, he just had to take it with both hands. "The the case was going some rounds," he said. "Just to make sure you learn the rounds. I last went the distance back in 2024. So, we did the sparring and we did the rounds and I've been tired of that work. And then in the ring, I said to myself, 'Actually,' I always say that, 'If there is a chance to finish it, I finish it. We don't know what's happening in two rounds.' So, he opened himself. I'm I said to myself, 'All right. Let's have a try.' That's it."

The 26-year-old is hoping to enjoy some sun before returning to the ring. Having fought mainly in Germany thus far, Jurk is itching to fight in the UK in front of his British fans, and is even eyeing a fight with fellow social media sensation and boxer Johnny Fisher. "I think first round KO for me, win first round," he said when asked about a fight with Fisher.

Article continues below

"He looks like he's a big puncher. But he's not a boxer. I saw the video clips how he spars the guy Eddie Hall. Man, now he spars him. How's Eddie Hall possible to hurt him? Like, how? He's probably got some power in himself, but I got bigger power in my hands. So, listen, I would like to fight him (Fisher), but I don't think that he takes the fight. Better for him."

Sports.title: ITV announce World Cup 2026 pundits with three ex-Man Utd players selected in huge line-up
Sports.content:
ITV announce World Cup 2026 pundits with three ex-Man Utd players selected in huge line-up

There are some notable omissions from ITV's World Cup team

View 3 Images Ian Wright, Gary Neville and Roy Keane will be part of ITV's punditry panel (Image: ITV)

Three former Manchester United players will be part of ITV's line-up at the World Cup. The broadcaster has unveiled a bumper team of pundits, presenters and commentators for the tournament in North America, which begins on June 11.

‌



It will include ex-United stars Roy Keane, Gary Neville and Juan Mata, along with an array of managers and former players. There will be two Arsenal legends in Patrick Vieira and Ian Wright, former Tottenham and Celtic boss Ange Postecoglou and ex-Rangers and Scotland hardman Duncan Ferguson.

‌



They will be joined by the manager of the US women's team, Emma Hayes, Lionesses legend Karen Carney, former Manchester City forward Bradley Wright-Phillips and regular Sky Sports pundit and ex-EFL star Jobi McAnuff.

‌



However, there is no place for Eni Aluko, who worked for ITV at the last World Cup, Euro 2024 and last year's women's Euros in Switzerland. Aluko subsequently complained that she was overlooked for the final between England and Spain, which Wright did work on.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

She had previously accused Wright of blocking opportunities for female pundits in women's football. There is also no place for Graeme Souness, Joe Cole, Nigel De Jong, Nadia Nadim, Hal Robson-Kanu, who worked for ITV at the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

‌



Coverage will be anchored by presenters Mark Pougatch, Laura Woods and Semra Hunter. Commentary will be led by Sam Matterface, Jon Champion, Seb Hutchinson and Joe Speight, with co-commentary provided by Lee Dixon, Ally McCoist, Andros Townsend and Lucy Ward. ITV's reporters on the ground will be Gabriel Clarke and Connie McLaughlin, while Christina Unkel will be the referee analyst.

Away from the serious analysis, a "third eye on the tournament, examining all of the biggest World Cup social and cultural moments," will be provided by Adam Richman, who will be joined by celebrity guests.

View 3 Images Eni Aluko fell out with Ian Wright over punditry opportunities (Image: 2022 Charlotte Wilson/Offside)

‌



As ever, ITV will share coverage with the BBC, while both channels will air the final. ITV will show the tournament's first two matches, including the opener between co-hosts Mexico City and South Africa in Mexico City.

They will also show England's first match against Croatia on Wednesday, June 17 (9pm BST) and the Three Lions' final group match against Panama on Saturday, June 27 (10pm BST). In between, ITV will show Scotland's middle group game against Morocco on Friday, June 19 (11pm BST).

ITV will also air the first matches involving world champions Argentina, Germany, the Netherlands and Spain. The network, which will show 29 group games in all, will broadcast live from New York City throughout the tournament.

‌



View 3 Images Laura Woods will be a key part of the ITV team (Image: Getty Images)

ITV director of sport Niall Sloane, said: "This is the biggest FIFA World Cup in history and we will be live from New York City for the duration of the tournament, bringing every key moment to life, free-to-air.

"Nothing unifies the UK audience more than a global sporting event and they don't come much bigger than this. Our broadcast line-up is second to none and our comprehensive coverage across ITV, ITVX, our World Cup 24/7 Channel, plus our digital platforms will ensure the ITV audience doesn't miss a second of action."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury confirms date for Anthony Joshua warm-up fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury confirms date for Anthony Joshua warm-up fight

The former two-time heavyweight champion returned to the ring last month after a long hiatus, but is targeting one more fight before taking on Anthony Joshua later this year

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will fight later this year (Image: Getty Images)

Tyson Fury admits he will fight again in August before taking on Anthony Joshua later this year.

‌



The 37-year-old agreed to a showdown with Joshua last month, just days after outpointing Arslanbek Makhmudov in north London. Fury's win marked his first appearance in the ring over a year after he announced his retirement following back-to-back defeats to Oleksandr Usyk in 2024.

‌



Joshua - who has not fought since knocking out Jake Paul last December - will make a return to competitive action on July 25, taking on Kristian Prenga in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Following news of the Brit's next fight, Fury himself has now decided he, too, would like another tune-up before trading leather with Joshua.

‌



Their money-spinning contest will likely take place in either October or November, but the two stars must first get through their respective fights. Touching on his immediate future, Fury plans on fighting again towards the end of summer. He recently revealed to FurociTV: "So my fight plan this year, with three fights. So it will be April, August and whenever the big fight is announced, either October or November.

Watch Oleksandr Usyk vs Rico Verhoeven live on DAZN This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £27.99 or £0 DAZN Order the fight here Product Description Oleksandr Usyk will fight Rico Verhoeven at the Pyramids of Giza on May 23 and boxing fans can watch the fight live on DAZN PPV for £27.99 and get one month of DAZN standard for free. Alternatively, the fight is included at no extra cost with DAZN Ultimate for £22.99 per month with a new introductory offer.

‌



"We have not got an opponent yet. But again. it’s never about the opponent, it’s just about me versus me always. So, whoever the opponent is, if it’s Joe Bloggs or if it’s Mike Tyson, it’s all important to me. It’s just a run out for me. Like, just to get sharper for the big one."

That said, Fury knows the risks of taking another fight before Joshua, insisting he could jeopardise the blockbuster bout should he get knocked out in August. He added: “Listen, I might get knocked out my next fight in August. So then it’s all over it. So I got to take one fight at a time, and they’re all deadly serious fights."

Tyson Fury explains exactly how he will beat Anthony Joshua READ MORE :

Tyson Fury explains why Anthony Joshua fight plan fell through READ MORE :

An opponent for Fury's next fight has yet to be confirmed. Fellow British heavyweight Dave Allen threw his name into the hat, but a clash between the pair looks doubtful after the 'White Rhino' was brutally knocked out by Filip Hrgovic in Doncaster last weekend.

Article continues below

In the same interview, Fury broke down his prediction for his fight with Joshua, and is confident he will send his bitter rival crashing to the canvas. "I’ll knock him out for sure. He will not be able to survive against me," he said. "He does not have any chin and I will bang him on it because I am quicker than him and I am a better boxer. So, the fun facts are this: Daniel Dubois' last five fights have been Usyk, ‘Big Baby’ Miller, Hrgovic, Joshua and Wardley. And out of all of those five men, he banged all of them on the jaw each time. And the only sucker to go down five times or even once was Joshua.

"He hit Usyk with everything right on the jaw - did not go over. Wardley the same. You saw it for ten, eleven rounds on the night. ‘Big Baby’ Miller was under total pressure the whole time. Did not go down once and so did Hrgovic, the same. The only one who got knocked out and knocked down five times was Joshua. So I will out him back in where he should be. Bambi on ice."

Sports.title: Aidan O’Brien pulls six out of Derby but still has 10 horses in £2m Classic
Sports.content:
Aidan O’Brien pulls six out of Derby but still has 10 horses in £2m Classic

The 11-time winner of the race still has a strong hand in the June 6 Epsom mile-and-a-half showpiece as the field was whittled down to 22

View 2 Images Aidan O'Brien (right): has ten entries in the 2026 Derby (Image: PA)

Aidan O’Brien has pulled six horses out of the £2 million Betfred Derby but still has a team of 10 in the Epsom Classic.

‌



The Ballydoyle trainer has a record 11 victories in the mile-and-a-half showpiece and is hot favourite to make it 12 on June 6.

His team is headed by Chester Vase winner Benvenuto Cellini who heads bookmakers’ ante-post market and is 2-1 with sponsors Betfred. Third favourite Constitution River, winner of the Dee Stakes at Chester, may be switched to the French Derby but Pierre Bonnard, a short head second in the Leopardstown Derby Trial, is expected to make the Epsom line-up.

‌



Paralysed former jockey left ‘devastated’ after car and vital specialist equipment stolen READ MORE :

Water To Wine, a 25-1 chance who was a late scratch from the Chester Vase, has been withdrawn by John and Thady Gosden. Saxon Street, winner of the Blue Riband Trial, could represent the stable depending on how he runs at Goodwood on Saturday.

Charlie Appleby will not be represented in either the Derby or Oaks after removing Del Maro, King’s Trail and Maho Bay from the colts’ race.

Article continues below

A field of 16 fillies remain in the Betfred Oaks, in which the market is headed by O’Brien paid Amelia Earhart and Precise.

Sports.title: Chelsea to file 'legal complaint' about Man City as Pep Guardiola replacement lined up
Sports.content:
Chelsea to file 'legal complaint' about Man City as Pep Guardiola replacement lined up

Pep Guardiola is set to leave Manchester City at the end of the season and former City coach and Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca is in line to replace him at the Etihad Stadium

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca could replace Pep Guardiola (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Chelsea are lining up a legal battle with Manchester City in the event that former boss Enzo Maresca is appointed as Pep Guardiola's replacement. City are faced with the stiff task of finding a successor for the Catalan coach, who is set to bring his Etihad career to an end after a decade at the club.

‌



Maresca is a leading contender for the role after departing Chelsea on New Year's Day in controversial circumstances. The Italian's position was deemed untenable as they parted via mutual consent.

‌



It was alleged that Maresca revealed to the club's hierarchy that he'd engaged in conversation with City over the possibility of replacing Guardiola. That claim has not been commented on by either club or disputed.

‌



While Maresca had previously guided Chelsea to Club World Cup glory, a run of one win in seven Premier League matches hinted at disquiet and saw the Blues fall away from second in the division. Maresca had also clashed with the board over transfers and demanded more senior players were signed before his departure.

The Telegraph now reports that Chelsea will seek compensation from City, using the terms of Maresca's exit from west London and the threat of disclosing the events in the months leading up to it. It is further stated that Chelsea would be required to bring a complaint to the Premier League for action to be taken against City.

Mirror Sport has approached both clubs for comment.

‌



Maresca did not conduct his post-match obligations following a draw with Bournemouth on December 30, and his departure arrived days later. There is said to be some frustration that the coach's early exit undermined the club's season.

Furious Pep Guardiola summons Man City stars in late-night summit to confirm exit READ MORE :

In December, following a win over Everton, Maresca put out a pointed jibe. Speaking in his post-match press conference, he said: "Since I joined the club, the last 48 hours have been the worst because many people didn't support us."

The Conference League-winning coach suggested it was meant 'in general' before noting he was 'very happy with the fans'.

‌



Maresca is a familiar face at City, having twice worked for the club. He spent time in charge of City's under-23s in 2020/21 and was an assistant to Guardiola in 2022/23 before he led Leicester to Championship glory and earned his move to Chelsea.

Guardiola was full of praise for Maresca following the Italian's exit and praised his own environment. “All I can say is that from my point of view Chelsea have lost an incredible manager and person,” he said.

“It’s a decision from the Chelsea hierarchy so I’ve nothing to say. How lucky I am in the club where I am. My club is extraordinary.”

It emerged on Monday that Guardiola was set to leave City after taking charge of matches against Bournemouth and Aston Villa. City are eyeing a final piece of silverware in the Premier League but require Arsenal to slip up for the former Barcelona star to add to his 20 trophies at the club.

The City boss will face the media for the first time since the news, this evening, as his side take on the Cherries.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
